analysis:
The PR is documentation-only. It modifies docs/reference/ssd-kv-cache.md by adding one table row (head line 375, "Active-store victim selection") that describes how the SSD prefix cache selects eviction victims. The row says selection is a linear oldest probe with a lexicographic tag tie-break. After a busy or undeletable candidate it takes one snapshot and walks a binary heap, at O(n) to build and O(log n) per candidate. External-removal reconciliation stops the pass so the budget can recheck usage. No source code, protocol, key handling, or configuration is changed in the supplied evidence.

Relevant model: T-041 (SSD prefix cache, SEC-035). The row concerns eviction order and availability only. It does not touch the TTL (still 1800 s, line 376), HMAC lookup-tag derivation, DBK3 AAD/metadata, the KEK purge, or the account-scoped cacheSalt. Nothing in the added text widens the at-rest surface or the TTFT oracle, and it does not change any documented mitigation.

Limits: the patch excerpt is truncated (patch_excerpt_complete=false), but the range map is complete with only head line 375 changed. I read the rest of the file, including the unchanged base text, only as surrounding context. The actual Swift implementation (SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.evictOldest, SSDBlockIndex.oldestFirstSnapshot) is not supplied, so the doc's accuracy and the cost of the snapshot under a large index are unverified. A reviewer of that code should check that the snapshot and heap path holds the removal lock for bounded time (the slice and lock behavior is documented at line 380) and that a stalled eviction cannot starve the lookup or donation paths. This is a question for the code change, not a finding on this doc.
